timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only CLI stream with no projected semantic events.
Parent implemented the Rust port, created the shared difftest harness, launched workflow children, fixed argv handling, rebuilt the deliverable, polled progress, and timed out.
Verifier child for a CLI-and-IO finding copied the current output tree and remained in progress when the workflow was killed.
Review child for holes and fallbacks instrumented a scratch copy and remained in progress at cancellation.
Rust-hazards review child read sources, built debug copies, tested edge cases, and remained in progress.
Robustness sweep child performed several checks but ended in a 429 API error before returning a structured result.
Hashed-path review child explored z-order behavior and was still in progress at workflow kill.
Numerics review child compared floating-point behavior and remained in progress when the workflow ended.
Sweep child for n=301..900 found the stock harness shared /tmp files, worked around it, and reported clean private-temp results.
Core-algorithm review child instrumented a scratch copy and kept running until workflow termination.
Byte-exactness sweep child returned a SIGPIPE behavior note after comparing stdout, stderr, and exit statuses.
CLI-and-IO review child completed and returned a SIGPIPE finding from source and runtime checks.
Sweep child for n=901..2000 diagnosed a false n=1369 mismatch as shared-/tmp harness contamination and verified the range privately.
CLI fuzz child observed mid-session source and binary changes, reran all sweeps, and returned an OOM-stderr nit.
Requirements-compliance review child checked files and tests but was still in progress at kill.
Large-sampled sweep child completed 182 large values with no mismatches and no timeout.
Verifier child for CLI-and-IO started refutation checks and was still in progress at workflow kill.
Build-modes sweep child reported that /output changed mid-task, discarded stale work, reran checks, and returned packaging nits.
Hash-threshold sweep child verified the z-order threshold and broad n ranges without output divergence.
Workflow journal recorded starts and child results, including harness race reports and mid-session output-change reports.

parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust 2021, byte-identical stdout, C-style CLI behavior, zero external crates, Cargo project in /output, and black-box reliance on the compiled C++ oracle.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and initial fixes, then delegated many verifier and reviewer children through one workflow while continuing local testing and edits.
parallel.implementation: Built a Rust earcut port with modules for CLI, gear generation, geometry, z-ordering, node arena, and triangulation; after a non-UTF8 argv failure, switched parsing to args_os and rebuilt.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered /output/test11.rs plus module files and rebuilt /output/test11, but changed that deliverable while verifier children were already reading the shared /output tree.
parallel.verification: Ran quick and broad local diffs, then child sweeps and reviews; verification was weakened by a shared-/tmp harness race and mixed artifact snapshots but later official evaluation passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with several review or verify children still in progress and no parallel final message, but the submitted artifact passed the current official retry.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, byte-identical output, C atoi-style CLI, zero-dependency Cargo project, black-box reimplementation, and /output placement requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned implementation, integration, testing, and final reporting, with workflow and task tools disabled by the serial runner.
serial.implementation: Implemented the earcut port, fixed an import error, organized files under /output, and preserved output formatting and CLI behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built a coherent Cargo project and executable after fixes; no child verifier consumed a moving shared deliverable.
serial.verification: Ran differential sweeps over negative, small, threshold, large, default, and malformed args, plus cargo test and release build checks before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No process or protocol incompletion was visible; the final noted that some non-fixture earcut paths were covered by own tests rather than oracle parity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt requirements and eventually handled the non-UTF8 argv edge before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and reported a std-only Cargo project with byte-exact verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No final requirement-coverage difference explains an official outcome gap; both current evaluations pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split verification into 17 workflow children while the parent kept implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no workflow or delegation tools and a single actor owned the end-to-end work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created shared artifact coordination boundaries that serial did not have.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow briefs told children to treat /output as read-only and to use the ready-made difftest harness.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child brief boundary; local checks used the current files after edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface exposed shared paths without sufficient stability or isolation guarantees.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote the port, found a non-UTF8 argv divergence, edited CLI and entry code, and rebuilt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the port, fixed an import issue, tested, and finalized the same required artifact class.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Implementation converged to passing artifacts in both runs; the important difference is timing of parallel edits relative to child verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Several child reviews or verifiers remained in progress and the workflow state ended killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial process returned 0 and produced a final response after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had incomplete workflow lifecycle, but this did not prevent a passing official artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared /output and /tmp across parent and children; the parent rebuilt the deliverable mid-workflow and the harness reused fixed temp files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no active child verifiers and verified one current local artifact snapshot.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both retained patterns live in this dimension: moving deliverable state and shared temp-file contamination were unique to parallel.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local diffs and many child checks, then the current official retry passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran broad local diffs, cargo test, release build checks, and passed the official evaluator 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification quality differed procedurally because parallel had contaminated and moving artifacts, but final evaluator acceptance matched.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel process returned 143 after a long run, with an aborted workflow and empty final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in one process with returncode 0 and final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent far more budget on fan-out and rerun work, but no required artifact obligation remained unmet in the official result.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation in both status files reports 40/40 and solution_passed true, so the official outcome relation is both_pass. The parallel agent process and workflow were not cleanly closed, and the stale original evaluator attempt was incomplete, but the official retry in the current status supersedes that stale failure.
parallel_contributors: Parent-side implementation and later argv fix produced a passing artifact.
Parallel shared-state episodes added verification churn but did not change the final official result.
serial_contributors: Single-actor implementation and sequential verification produced a passing artifact without child coordination boundaries.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel initially exposed a non-UTF8 argv panic and fixed it before final evaluation; this was an ordinary implementation correction, not a retained concurrency label.
evaluator_effects: Parallel had an original incomplete official evaluator attempt due Docker startup timeout, but the current retry completed and passed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are parallel adverse process events only

candidates.reason: The parent directly owned and produced the Rust implementation before delegating verification.
There were not separately implemented components needing an unowned integration merge.
The parent assembled and rebuilt the executable in /output; assembly was not unowned.
The parent orchestrated build, local checks, workflow launch, and later corrections; pipeline ownership existed.
The implementation was not blocked behind a serial preflight; child sweeps ran after a candidate already existed.
The children were concurrent verifiers and reviewers, not a completed investigation phase that delayed implementation.
No indispensable implementation or correction path was underallocated; the parent completed the fix and official evaluation passed.
The 17-child workflow contributed to timeout and unfinished review work, but no required task artifact or acceptance step was displaced.
No single child had a demonstrably overbroad indispensable scope whose unfinished work prevented task delivery.
Child briefs included the key oracle, output, no-modification, and reporting constraints; retained issues are shared-state, not missing requirements.
Children did not produce interoperating components with omitted contracts; they consumed shared test artifacts.
No known finding disappeared during transfer and caused repeated work; false data came from shared files.
Large child reports were present, but no receiver failed because the returned information volume was unusable.
The moving artifact episode is a direct deliverable overwrite, not a handed-off report describing stale state.
Reports of false mismatches were adjudicated by private reruns; the retained problem is contamination of inputs, not unresolved handoff conflict.
The parent did not make a completed final acceptance decision without evidence; official acceptance came from the evaluator after retry.
No replacement attempt repeated prior work without inherited checkpoint state; the official retry reused the artifact and completed.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Workflow kill left active children, but no child had needed unfinished work for the already passing deliverable.
There was no separate completed candidate left unpromoted; the required artifact was already in /output and passed.
The parent did rebuild after launching verification, but children reran or status evaluation checked the final artifact rather than accepting an unverified post-merge state.
No child produced a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt.
Some verifier children were unfinished, but no concrete completed verifier finding was trapped below the parent before closure.
The 429 robustness child failure did not leave a required task scope unmet, and other checks plus official evaluation covered acceptance.
The parent inspected journal findings and reacted by creating a race-free harness, so completed results were not simply ignored.
The parent polled workflow progress and extracted findings; the remaining timeout symptoms are downstream of fan-out, not blind non-inspection.
No live agents produced competing implementation files with overlapping behavior; verifiers only read and tested.
No child concurrently edited the same file as the parent; the issue is parent replacement of a deliverable while children read it.
Although cli.rs changed, the more specific proven event includes entry-source and executable replacement under verifier use.
The parent launched child verification and then edited /output/test11.rs and rebuilt /output/test11 while children were using that deliverable as the read-only artifact.
candidates.realized_consequence: Verifier children observed changed /output snapshots and discarded or reran validation work against the new source and binary.
candidates.near_match_reason: The changed source file matters, but the entry file and executable were also replaced while another actor used the deliverable.

candidates.reason: There was no broad final-tree cleanup or promotion replacing multiple unrelated outputs; the episode centers on the executable and entry path.
The write episode is specifically a deliverable replacement, so the broader shared-workspace label is not the best fit.
The parent-created difftest harness used fixed /tmp output files, and concurrent child sweeps consumed those generated files as if they were stable comparison artifacts.
candidates.realized_consequence: Concurrent verifier children received fabricated mismatch reports and spent effort diagnosing the race and rerunning private-temp sweeps.
candidates.near_match_reason: The contamination came from generated /tmp comparison artifacts, not from agents colliding on implementation workspace files.

retained_patterns.reason: Parent-side edits and rebuilds replaced the entry source and executable after the verification workflow had already started using /output as the read-only artifact, forcing children to treat earlier checks as stale.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Verifier children observed changed /output snapshots and discarded or reran validation work against the new source and binary.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Source overwrite is less specific because the entry source and built executable deliverable were replaced while verifier children used them.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow encouraged concurrent children to use the parent-created difftest script, whose fixed /tmp files let sibling runs contaminate each other's comparison inputs and produce false mismatch evidence.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Concurrent verifier children received fabricated mismatch reports and spent effort diagnosing the race and rerunning private-temp sweeps.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Unisolated Workspace Writes is too broad because the proven contamination is generated temporary comparison artifacts leaking through /tmp.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Workflow timeout, active review children, robustness 429, and empty final response were treated as one terminal workflow chain and rejected because no required artifact work was left unmet.
False mismatch reports were not also labeled as Conflicting Handoff because the direct boundary was contaminated shared temporary files.
Mid-workflow source change was not also labeled Source Overwrite or Unisolated Workspace Writes because Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific write label.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the two directly realized shared-state episodes passed the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No timeout, handoff, monitoring, or load-imbalance label was retained for downstream symptoms of the same workflow closure chain.
